results.topic: Whether streaming has killed the theatrical experience

result.text: Streaming hasn’t killed theaters, but it shifted my frame of reference. Sitting on my couch offers comfort, yet nothing replaces the collective breath held in a darkened room. Convenience is nice, but I deeply miss the sheer magic of genuine communal cinema. 3.5/5

results.topic: The Brutalist and its 3.5 hour runtime

result.text: I spent three and a half hours absorbing The Brutalist, and I found it to be a genuinely mixed bag. The ambition is staggering, yet the narrative suffers from tonal whiplash in the final stretch. Still, my frame of reference for cinema demands this kind of scale. 3.5/5

Superhero fatigue is real, but not because the genre itself is broken. I felt it deeply this weekend. It is a mixed bag of corporate overextension and increasingly comic-booky storytelling that lacks any grounding frame of reference. 2.5/5.

Greig Fraser’s cinematography in Dune Part Two is a stunning mixed bag. While some sequences feel overly digital and comic-booky, the vast desert frames completely overwhelmed my senses. It is an undervalued visual achievement that demands the biggest screen possible. 4/5
